subject: Model evals follow-up: open models vs PayGrid baseline
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@paygrid.com>, Sara Liu <sara.liu@paygrid.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model evals follow-up: open models vs PayGrid baseline

Hi Tom / Sara — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned: 

Key points from today's discovery:
- PayGrid wants a model that matches your existing proprietary baseline on accuracy for payment routing intents (intent F1) and entity extraction (NER F1).
- Primary constraints: latency <= 250ms P95 for single-turn routing calls, and model outputs must not regress >2% relative to your baseline on core benchmarks.
- Data: sample payloads and the current baseline metrics export (CSV) would help us run targeted evals.

What we'll do from Redwood side:
- Run targeted model-fit evals across a short list of open models + optimized quantized variants, using your prompt sets and our standard benchmark harness.
- Share evaluation artifacts: per-prompt performance, latency traces, and suggested prompt/temperature adjustments.
- Propose a mutual action plan (MAP) with acceptance thresholds and a PoC timeline.

Ask from PayGrid: can you share: 1) the baseline metrics export (CSV), 2) 100-200 representative prompts (anonymized), and 3) the definition of "parity" you want to use (F1 delta, top-k accuracy, etc.)? If you can drop those into the Drive folder we linked in the call, we’ll start evaluations tomorrow.

Attaching the brief evaluation plan we mentioned (pdf stub).

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-reco-models-0319.pdf (evaluation plan stub)

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@paygrid.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Liu <sara.liu@paygrid.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model evals follow-up: open models vs PayGrid baseline

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. We're onboard to share materials. Attaching our baseline CSV and a small prompt set (anonymized). A few clarifications: 

- Baseline metrics: attached CSV contains per-intent F1 and per-entity F1 aggregated over our validation slices. The teams have historically considered parity to mean <=1.5% absolute drop for intent F1 and <=2% for NER F1, but we'd be willing to accept up to 2% across the board if latency gains are material.
- Proprietary baseline: our in-house model benefits from dataset-specific pretraining and some task-specific heuristics — important to call out when comparing to general open models.
- Please prioritize models known for strong NER and short-context instruction-following. We're especially interested in any 7B/13B open architectures you recommend.

Pls see attachments: paygrid-baseline-metrics-0320.csv, paygrid-sample-prompts-0320.txt

Tom
Tom Ellis
Director, ML Engineering | PayGrid

Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model evals follow-up: open models vs PayGrid baseline

Thanks Tom — got the CSV and prompt set. I ran a quick smoke eval overnight against three recommended open models (7B and 13B variants) and a lightweight quantized 13B. Early findings (very preliminary):

- model-gemini-7b-open: intent F1 delta = -3.2%, NER F1 delta = -4.0% (falls short of parity)
- model-lucent-13b: intent F1 delta = -1.1%, NER F1 delta = -1.8% (within your stated 1.5–2% threshold)
- model-aurora-13b-quant8: intent F1 delta = -1.9%, NER F1 delta = -2.1% (close for intents, slightly over for NER)

Latency (single-request, optimized pipeline):
- lucent-13b: P95 ~230ms (meets 250ms target)
- aurora-13b-quant8: P95 ~180ms (excellent latency)

Notes: the provisional results suggest a 13B open model (lucent-13b) comes close to parity on both metrics and meets latency. Gap for NER on aurora quantized is small and might be addressed by prompt tuning or a lightweight fine-tune on the anonymized NER labels.

Next steps I propose:
1) Full eval run across your full prompt set + slice breakdowns (labels: payment types, edge cases).
2) Prompt-set tuning and one-pass few-shot prefix adjustments.
3) If required, a short targeted fine-tune (up to ~10k anonymized examples) to hit NER parity.

I’ve uploaded the full smoke CSV and the evaluation harness link here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ExampleBenchmark
And I added the HubSpot deal note: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/PG-7892

Happy to jump on a quick sync this week to walk through the CSV and acceptance thresholds.

—Aditya

Subject: Re: Model evals follow-up: security and data handling questions

Hi Tom / Sara — quick security items while we kick off evals: 

- Data handling: for the sample prompts and metrics you share, we recommend anonymizing PII. Confirm whether the attached CSV has been redacted; if not, we’ll treat it as limited-scope and use the Private evaluation pipeline.
- Retention: by default, evaluation artifacts created in our hosted eval runs are stored for 30 days; we can extend or disable retention for PoC.
- On-prem / VPC: If you prefer we can run the eval harness in your VPC or with a Private deployment to ensure no telemetry leaves your environment. That adds ~2–3 extra days to setup.
- Compliance docs: attaching a stub pointing to our SOC 2 and data handling overview (links). Please let us know if you need an NDA amendment.

Attachment: redwood-compliance-stub.pdf

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Security Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@paygrid.com>, Sara Liu <sara.liu@paygrid.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model evals follow-up: open models vs PayGrid baseline — proposed MAP

Tom / Sara — thanks for the quick turnaround and for sharing the baseline. Based on Aditya’s smoke run and the security notes, here’s a proposed mutual action plan and acceptance thresholds to unblock a short PoC: 

Mutual Action Plan (proposed):
1) Materials Ingest (by Mar 23): PayGrid uploads the full prompt set + baseline CSV to the shared Drive folder and confirms anonymization level.
2) Full Eval Run (Mar 24–26): Redwood runs full eval on 3 candidate models (lucent-13b, aurora-13b-quant8, and a safety-optimized 13B). Deliverables: per-prompt performance, slice breakdowns, latency traces, and a short playbook for prompt tweaks.
3) Prompt tuning pass (Mar 27–28): Redwood tries prompt-set tuning and few-shot prefixes to recover NER deltas under threshold.
4) Optional targeted fine-tune (Mar 29–Apr 2): If parity still not reached, run a short fine-tune on up to 10k anonymized examples (only with PayGrid approval).
5) PoC decision (Apr 3): joint review. If parity achieved (see thresholds) and latency constraints met, proceed to pilot rollout discussion (Dedicated or Private).

Acceptance thresholds (proposed):
- Intent F1: no more than 2.0% absolute drop vs your baseline
- NER F1: no more than 2.0% absolute drop vs your baseline
- Latency: P95 <= 250ms in optimized inference pipeline

Security / Ops notes:
- If PayGrid requests Private evaluation (VPC/on-prem), we can set that up; it will add ~2–3 days to the timeline.
- Evaluation artifacts retention will default to 30 days unless you request extension.

If this looks good, I’ll lock the dates in the MAP and we’ll start the full eval on Mar 24. Would you prefer a brief 30-min sync Monday morning to review the smoke CSV or should we proceed directly?

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
